notes: v1.14.544 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 4: THE LEGACY HOST NET IS CUT. deploy_opsHost() no longer falls through to #ops-content when the redesign's #wk-deploy is missing; it warns and returns null. ⭐ The fallback was never a safety net — it was a dead-render host. #ops-content lives inside pg-sop, which the redesign never shows, so falling back rendered the deploy surface into a hidden node and reported success to every caller. v1.14.224 already fixed one instance by hand (vendorEdp_open, its own note says 'invisible 100% of the time'); this fixes the source instead of the symptom, so a missing host is now SAYABLE rather than silent. ⛔ THE LEGACY RETURN IS NOT REMOVED, and cutting it would have been the obvious misreading of this stage: under ?legacy=1 #ops-content is the CORRECT host, not a net. It stays until Stage 7 deletes the legacy house. Only the redesign branch loses its fallthrough. One caller needed the guard that honesty implies: deploy_showList took `container || deploy_opsHost()` and used it unchecked, so a legitimate null would have thrown at container.innerHTML. It now fails loud in the shape v1.14.461 established for rack detail — say what is wrong and where to go, and never leave body state half-set as though navigation happened. mscope_renderStaged and deploy_showCommandCenter already guarded. ⚠ NOTHING CHANGES IN NORMAL USE, in either house: #wk-deploy is mounted under the redesign and #ops-content under legacy, so both resolve exactly as before. This ship only changes what happens when the app is ALREADY broken — the difference between a silent dead render and a toast that names the fault.
